_readme.what: Routing-oriented model knowledge base for AI agents and the Model Intelligence panel. The panel is a typeset rendering of THIS file — same ids, same values. As an agent, read this whole object before routing: pick a model by matching a task against each model's bestFor (and not avoidFor), then break ties by price (price.inputPerM/outputPerM, USD per million tokens — lower is cheaper), speed (speedTps, output tokens/sec — higher is faster/lower-latency), context (max input window in tokens — bigger fits more code/docs), and benchmarks (benchmarks.aaIndex is the headline intelligence score, higher = smarter; sweBench/lmarenaElo for coding).
_readme.howAgentsUse: 1) Filter models to roster.inPlay===true (the user's hard gate — never route to an out-of-roster or status==='fading' model). 2) Match the task to bestFor and exclude any avoidFor. 3) Use tier ('frontier' = top intelligence, 'fast' = low-latency cheap, 'open' = open-weight value, 'specialist' = task-tuned) and the `routing` rules to choose. 4) Break ties with price/speedTps/context/benchmarks. 5) For multi-model work, match orchestration.taskShapeRules by priority, resolve recipe roles against roster.inPlay, and fall back to routing.default when a recipe is unresolvable. Quote `freshness.snapshot.curatedAsOf` when citing sentiment/benchmarks/speedTps; price and context may be fresher (see `freshness.live`). Consult `picks` for fast canned routing (smartest / proFavorite / fastest / cheapest / rising).
_readme.fieldProvenance: OpenRouter live data covers price.inputPerM, price.outputPerM, and context only. speedTps and every other field are curated and dated to freshness.snapshot.curatedAsOf. Per-model `liveFields` records what actually merged this render; fetchedAt null means nothing has merged and all baked model liveFields must be empty.
_readme.humanControl: roster.inPlay is the ONLY user-authored field (localStorage key claude-os-model-roster). It is the agent's hard gate — do not route where inPlay===false.

rules: Hardest reasoning / multi-file refactor → highest benchmarks.aaIndex frontier model with roster.inPlay===true.
High-volume or latency-critical → cheapest in-roster model with speedTps>=80 and tier in ['fast','open'].
Never route where roster.inPlay===false or status==='fading'.
Multi-step or high-stakes work → use the orchestration block (taskShapeRules → recipes); fall back to routing.default when a recipe cannot resolve.

orchestration._readme: Match taskShapeRules by priority, resolve every recipe role using eligible roster.inPlay candidates, and fall back to routing.default if the recipe cannot resolve.
